newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai Soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Tuesday on profit-taking mainly from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded May 1997 contract ended at 3,430 yuan ($413) per tonne, rising 30 yuan. It opened at 3,420 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,350 and a high of 3,435.
July fell 50 yuan to 3,210, September 30 to 3,348, November one to 3,395 and the January 1998 contract seven to 3,392.
Combined volume fell to 21,300 tonnes from 30,400.
Soybeans opened little changed but profit-taking pushed prices down for most of the session, traders said.
"Profit-taking from retail investors dominated today's trading," one traders said.
"Soybean trading is likely to remain dull with prices consolidating around current levels because the booming stock markets have attracted most of the hot money," he said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the next few days.
